# Education in Finland
## Basic and Upper Secondary Education
Finland's compulsory education system is comprehensive, covering grades 1 to 9 (the *peruskoulu* ), and has recently expanded to include upper secondary school (grades 10–12) and vocational school. The system emphasizes that there are no "gifted" programs, with advanced students expected to assist those who are slower to learn. All schools up to the university level are predominantly funded and administered by municipalities. While private schools exist, tuition fees are strictly prohibited, and selective admission is not permitted; they must offer the same social benefits as municipal schools. Teachers are fully unionized, adhere to state curriculum guidelines, but are given significant autonomy regarding instructional methods and textbook selection. Learning is supported by small class sizes, and extracurricular activities are stressed alongside minimal homework.

# Education in Finland
## Tertiary and Adult Education
Tertiary education is divided into traditional universities ( *yliopisto, universitet* ) and universities of applied sciences ( *ammattikorkeakoulu* ). Admissions are merit-based, transparent, and objective, relying on high school final GPA, final exams, and entrance examinations, with no weighting given to extracurricular activities. Universities focus on theoretical science research, while universities of applied sciences are more practical and geared towards industry needs. Adult education includes *vapaa sivistystyö* ("Free Education"), which offers non-professional courses to support personality development, and the *kansalaisopisto* (Citizens' Institutes), which are often municipal evening institutions offering humanities and language courses at modest tuition fees.
